sections.h2: Who does what on a Bay County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Bay County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, local governments set millage rates, and the Bay County Tax Collector prints, mails and collects the bill.

The Tax Collector's real estate page describes the sequence: the appraiser assesses, the County Commission and other levying bodies set millage, the appraiser builds the roll, and the certified roll goes to the Tax Collector. Any change to name, mailing address, location or assessed value has to go through the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector. Owners who pay through escrow should know the mortgage company requests the original bill and the owner gets a copy.

  • Property Appraiser: value questions and TRIM notice questions, (850) 248-8401 per the Value Adjustment Board page.
  • Tax Collector: payment, delinquent tax and tax deferral.
  • Clerk of Court and Comptroller: records and the Value Adjustment Board clerk work.

sections.h2: Where can I pay Bay County property tax in person?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector lists four service offices, and a Bay County bill can only be paid at its own offices.

  • Panama City: 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, FL 32401.
  • Panama City Beach: 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, FL 32407.
  • Lynn Haven: 700 Florida Ave., Lynn Haven, FL 32444.
  • Callaway: 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy, Callaway, FL 32404.

Bring the property tax notice or the property address. Delinquent taxes must be paid with certified funds, which the page defines as cash, cashier's check, money order or credit card. Appointments are available through the Tax Collector's site, and you can also pay online.

sections.h2: When are Bay County taxes due, and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Notices are normally mailed on or before November 1, the due date is March 31, and anything unpaid becomes delinquent April 1.

Early payment discounts on the Bay County Tax Collector real estate page
Payment monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%

Non-ad valorem assessments, mainly paving, stormwater and solid waste collection, are collected on the same schedule: billed from November 1, delinquent April 1, with early payment discounts. They come from local governments and are certified to the Tax Collector, so a question about one goes to the government that levied it.

sections.h2: How do I file for homestead or other exemptions in Bay County?
sections.html:
File with the Bay County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the tax year, having made the home your permanent residence by January 1.

The Tax Collector's page is explicit that exemptions must be applied for through the Property Appraiser. State rules say the homestead exemption is worth up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes too and the second $25,000 applying only above $50,000 of assessed value and only to non-school levies.

  • Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or CPI. The state chart shows a 2.7 percent cap for 2026.
  • A sale or foreclosure resets the property to just value on the next January 1.
  • A seller who rents the home out loses homestead, with a limited carve-out for servicemembers.

The Value Adjustment Board page adds that a timely filed homestead application that was denied needs no petition fee, while one received after March 1 does.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Bay County assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Bay County Value Adjustment Board. The 2026 petition deadline was September 8, 2026, and that date has passed, so the next window opens after the next TRIM notices in August.

Bay County Value Adjustment Board filing details as printed on its site
ItemDetail
Filing fee$50.00, non-refundable
Online filingAdds a 3.5% non-refundable card processing fee
Extra contiguous parcels or accounts$5.00 for each after the first
Mail address for checks225 McKenzie Avenue, Panama City, FL 32401

Section 194.014, quoted on that page, requires a petitioner contesting value to pay all non-ad valorem assessments and at least 75 percent of the ad valorem taxes, less the discount, before the taxes go delinquent. If the partial payment is missed, the board must deny the petition by April 20.

sections.h2: What can a Bay County owner do about a bill they cannot pay?
sections.html:
Florida law offers a homestead tax deferral, filed on Form DR-570 with the Tax Collector by March 31, covering tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident aged 65 or older.

An owner can also apply for the installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year under section 197.222. Ask the Bay County Tax Collector which plans it runs and what the payoff is.

If taxes stay unpaid, they turn delinquent April 1 and the state requires tax certificates to be sold by June 1. After two years from April 1 of the issue year, the holder may apply for a tax deed. A seller in that position can usually resolve the balance from the sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What happens to Bay County tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
The owner of record on the roll gets the bill, and the buyer and seller divide the year at closing. Ask the title company for the current bill, any non-ad valorem balance and the discount month in effect.

Florida charges a deed documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, paid to the clerk at recording. All parties to a taxable deed are liable, whoever agrees to pay.

A buyer starts at just value the next January 1 with no inherited cap, so the seller's tax history is a poor guide to what the buyer will owe. Selling an inherited or storm-worn house works the same way: clear liens and unpaid balances first, then record the deed in Panama City.

faqs.q: What is the Bay County property tax due date?
faqs.a: March 31. Taxes become delinquent April 1, and bills are normally mailed on or before November 1.

faqs.q: How much is the Bay County early payment discount?
faqs.a: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, with none in March.

faqs.q: Where is the Bay County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: The main office is at 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, with branches in Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway. Bring your notice or property address.

faqs.q: Can I still file a 2026 value petition in Bay County?
faqs.a: The 2026 deadline was September 8, 2026, and petitions after it are treated as late filed and subject to review. Call the Property Appraiser at (850) 248-8401 with questions.

faqs.q: Does a Bay County buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A change of ownership resets the property to just value the following January 1, with exceptions such as certain transfers between spouses.
